questions.q: What distinguishes a filter modifier function from a plain CALCULATE filter argument?
options: It changes how filtering itself behaves, rather than adding a simple condition
It only works inside calculated columns
It can only be used with text columns
It removes the need for a relationship between tables
questions.explain: Functions like REMOVEFILTERS, KEEPFILTERS, and USERELATIONSHIP change the mechanics of filtering, rather than narrowing rows with a Boolean condition.

questions.q: In '%Sales = DIVIDE([TotalSales], CALCULATE([TotalSales], REMOVEFILTERS()))', what does REMOVEFILTERS() do?
options: Clears every filter, giving the denominator the grand total regardless of what's selected
Removes the TotalSales measure from the model
Adds a filter that overwrites what's currently active
Only clears filters from numeric columns
questions.explain: REMOVEFILTERS with no arguments clears all filters, so the denominator always reflects the full, unfiltered total — the standard building block for a percent-of-total measure.

questions.q: What does KEEPFILTERS change about CALCULATE's default behavior?
options: It makes a new filter combine (intersect) with an existing one instead of overwriting it
It permanently deletes all other filters in the model
It converts the measure into a calculated column
It has no effect — it's purely for documentation
questions.explain: Normally CALCULATE's filter overwrites an existing filter on the same column. KEEPFILTERS makes the two filters apply together instead, using their intersection.

questions.q: What does USERELATIONSHIP let a measure do?
options: Use a specific inactive relationship for just that one calculation
Create a brand new relationship on the fly
Delete a relationship permanently
Convert an active relationship into a calculated column
questions.explain: USERELATIONSHIP activates a normally-inactive relationship for a single calculation, without changing which relationship is active by default in the model.

questions.q: What modeling pattern relies directly on USERELATIONSHIP?
options: Role-playing dimensions, like a single Date table used for order date, ship date, and delivery date
Snowflake dimensions
Junk dimensions
Many-to-many bridging tables
questions.explain: A role-playing dimension has one active relationship by default, with USERELATIONSHIP used in specific measures to reach the other, inactive relationships on demand.
